candidate.title: eventmanager.update swallows errors and returns [] when calendarReference is undefined
reports: [bug] the new catch block returns calendarreference?.map(...) ?? [], which is an empty array for any error thrown before calendarreference is assigned (e.g., the newbookingid lookup at the top of the try). a prisma/db failure during reschedule now resolves to an empty result list that callers treat as 'no calendar references to update', so the reschedule completes in the database without any calendar update and without the success:false failure entry the old catch returned — the failure signal is gone.

[advisory] the updateallcalendarevents catch block drops console.error(message) and now returns calendarreference?.map(...) ?? [], so an error thrown before calendarreference is assigned yields zero result rows and no log line, where the pre-diff code always emitted one failure row plus a log. calendar update failures occurring outside per-credential handling (e.g., the prisma lookup of the new booking) leave no trace anywhere and return an empty array that callers scanning for unsuccessful rows read as success — a rescheduled booking silently keeps its stale calendar event with nothing to debug.

[bug] the rewritten catch in eventmanager's update path drops the console.error(message) that previously recorded failures, and returns calendarreference?.map(...) ?? [], which is an empty array whenever the throw happens before calendarreference is assigned (e.g. the newbooking prisma lookup inside the same try). a database failure during a reschedule/update is now returned as an empty result list — indistinguishable from 'no calendar references to update' — with no log line at all, so the caller proceeds as if nothing needed updating, the calendar event is left stale, and the failure is invisible to both the user and operators.
